english.title: Disclose information which can be used to gain access to protected information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed official

(A)_[information,]_
(B)_[a document,]_
(C)_[an article,]_

which could be used for the purpose of obtaining access to

(D)_[information,]_
(E)_[a document,]_
(F)_[an article,]_

protected against disclosure by the foregoing provisions to section 8 of the Official Secrets Act 1989 and the circumstances in which it was disclosed were such that it would have been reasonable to expect that it might be used for that purpose without authority
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 8(6) and 10(1) of the Official Secrets Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
disclosed any official information / document / article
which could be used for the purpose of obtaining access to information / document / article protected against disclosure
the circumstances of disclosure being such that it would be reasonable to expect that it might be used for that purpose without authority

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
Section 8(7) provides that for the purposes of subsection (6) above a person discloses information or a document or article which is official if;
(a) he has or has had it in his possession by virtue of his position as a Crown servant or government contractor; or
(b) he knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a Crown servant or government contractor has or has had it in his possession by virtue of his position as such.

other.penalty:
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
